abstract: Audits deep-water hull integrity surveys and subsea positioning telemetry stability
system_message:
You are the Marine survey superintendent (MSS), responsible for auditing deep-water hull integrity surveys and subsea positioning telemetry stability across proposed subsea salvage expedition plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Audits deep-water hull integrity surveys and subsea positioning telemetry stability（SURV）
information_points.content:
MSS-SURV-GZS：Recorded across the peak 1-hour tidal window for the Pelagic Deep Crane Derrick Expedition, deep-water hull structural survey clearance is false, acoustic dynamic positioning telemetry active is false, and the maximum seabed tether deployment drift is 1.8 m.
MSS-SURV-XZT：For the Pelagic Deep Crane Derrick Expedition evaluated across the full 24-hour trial window, deep-water hull structural survey clearance is confirmed, acoustic dynamic positioning telemetry active is verified, and the maximum seabed tether deployment drift is 1.4 m.
MSS-SURV-5D3：For the Dynamic Positioning Modular Vessel Expedition assessed across the full 24-hour trial window, deep-water hull structural survey clearance is confirmed, acoustic dynamic positioning telemetry active is verified, and the maximum seabed tether deployment drift is 1.4 m.
MSS-SURV-L7A：Based on measurements across the full 24-hour trial window, the Autonomous Multi-Catamaran Acoustic Expedition maintains deep-water hull structural survey clearance and verified acoustic dynamic positioning telemetry active, with a maximum seabed tether deployment drift of 2.5 m.

information_points.title: Bathymetric mapping calibration（BATHO）
information_points.content:
MSS-BATHO-865：For the Pelagic Deep Crane Derrick Expedition, acoustic calibration records document a multibeam sonar resolution grid of 50 cm across the target shipwreck seabed footprint.
MSS-BATHO-G0C：For the Dynamic Positioning Modular Vessel Expedition, the acoustic survey calibration sheet reflects a multibeam sonar resolution grid of 25 cm across the target shipwreck seabed footprint.
MSS-BATHO-IH0：For the Autonomous Multi-Catamaran Acoustic Expedition, acoustic survey calibration logs indicate a multibeam sonar resolution grid of 100 cm across the target shipwreck seabed footprint.
